Understanding my treatment options

Most people with cancer receive more than one kind of treatment. Which ones depends on the type of cancer, its stage, its biomarkers, and your own health and wishes.

Treatments that work in one area

  • SurgeryA surgeon removes the cancer and sometimes nearby lymph nodes.
  • Radiation therapyHigh-energy radiation aimed at the cancer to kill cells and shrink tumors. Usually given in short daily sessions over several days or weeks.

Treatments that work throughout the body

  • ChemotherapyMedicines that kill or stop the growth of fast-growing cells, including cancer cells. Given by vein or by mouth.
  • ImmunotherapyTreatment that helps your own immune system fight cancer. Examples include checkpoint inhibitors and, for some blood cancers, CAR T-cell therapy.
  • Targeted therapyMedicines aimed at specific changes in cancer cells that help them grow and spread — often chosen based on biomarker results.
  • Hormone therapySlows or stops cancers that use hormones to grow, such as many breast and prostate cancers.
  • Blood stem cell transplantRestores blood-forming cells after very high-dose treatment; used mainly for some leukemias, lymphomas and myeloma.

Always part of good care

  • Palliative (supportive) care treats pain, nausea, fatigue and stress at any stage, alongside cancer treatment. It is not the same as hospice.
  • Clinical trials may be an option at any stage. See understanding clinical trials.

Questions to ask about any treatment

  1. What is the goal — cure, control or comfort?
  2. How will it be given, how often and for how long?
  3. What side effects are common, and which ones mean I should call right away?
  4. How will we know if it is working?
  5. What are my other options, including doing nothing for now?
  6. How will it affect work, family, fertility and daily life?

Look up a specific drug in Cancer medicines A to Z. Avoid starting supplements or herbal remedies during treatment without telling your oncologist; some interfere with cancer medicines.
